GROUNDING (plan-review E4/T8): the plan conflated TWO distinct multi-attempt mechanisms. Verified in code (worktree at S3 tip):

MECHANISM A — FallbackModel candidates (model_classes.build_fallback_model, model_classes.py:414-434): builds FallbackModel(*models), candidates with N+1 concrete models (primary first). FallbackModel iterates candidates WITHIN ONE agent.run; pydantic-ai counts ONE model-request/turn. These are the candidate CHILD spans under one logical Agent-request span (AC-1, AC-2).

MECHANISM B — native->prompted downgrade (structured_run._pai_structured, structured_run.py:118-145): calls _run_native_output (agent.run_sync #1, structured_run.py:210) and, on a 895c grammar-compilation rejection, _run_prompted_output (agent.run_sync #2, structured_run.py:248). This is TWO SEPARATE Agent runs => TWO Agent-request spans (native attempt RAISED, prompted attempt RETURNED), a distinct orchestration-layer mechanism — NOT a FallbackModel candidate, and it DOES add a second Agent request by design. Each of those two runs may itself contain Mechanism-A candidate child spans.

Consequence: AC-3 must stop claiming 'candidate outcomes without adding an Agent request' and instead verify two distinct logical-turn spans from the downgrade, instrumented at the _pai_structured boundary (Scope must add structured_run.py).

Also grounded: pydantic-ai 1.107.2 exposes NO public InstrumentedModel; the Agent model-request span is pydantic_ai._instrumentation.open_model_request_span (active under setup_tracing/Agent.instrument_all). S4 candidate spans nest beneath it via the ambient OTel span context and reuse runner.py provenance (provider_provenance['candidates'], runner.py:458-463). tracing.py today only exposes setup_tracing() (OTel TracerProvider + instrument_all), lazy-imported => lean-import safe. No in-memory-exporter test exists yet; a new test uses opentelemetry InMemorySpanExporter.

Plan v3 now REUSES InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel for candidate spans rather than a bespoke tracer (resolves T1).

Also resolved: (a) prerequisite-consistency vs S2 — S4 makes NO _pai_structured change; it only OBSERVES the S2-preserved bug-895c native->prompted fallback (S2 AC-7). Both the native and prompted agent.run route through the same wrapped candidates, so the downgrade is legible as native-span raised then prompted-span returned with zero control-flow change. Dropped structured_run.py from scope/file_impact; removed all 'adds a second Agent run by design' language. (b) T8 sanitization — raised-reason text now routed through the existing rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic allowlist. compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Pydantic deliberately counts one Agent-visible model turn even when `FallbackModel` tries multiple candidates inside it. The approved RP-01 decision follows maintained-project practice: keep that request budget authoritative and make candidate activity operationally visible as tracing, not as `candidate_requests` in usage. `Agent.instrument_all()` (already called by `setup_tracing`, `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py:54`) instruments only the Agent's OUTER model — for a fallback run that is the `FallbackModel`, yielding ONE model-request span whose internal candidate iteration is invisible. Candidate construction is centralized in `model_classes.build_fallback_model` (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:414+`); `runner.PydanticAIRunner` already records ordered candidate provenance (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:372-465`). This story is purely additive instrumentation and does NOT change the S2 `_pai_structured` control flow, whose one bounded operation already preserves the bug-895c native-to-prompted fallback (S2 AC-7).

## Approach
Make each candidate visible by wrapping every already-built concrete candidate model (inside `build_fallback_model`) in a thin subclass of pydantic-ai's own `pydantic_ai.models.wrapper.WrapperModel`. Its `request` override opens ONE rebar-owned child span — via `opentelemetry.trace.get_tracer(...).start_as_current_span(...)` on the SAME `TracerProvider` that `setup_tracing`/`instrument_all` already configures (not a parallel tracer) — around `super().request(...)`. It reuses the library's wrapping primitive but does NOT use `InstrumentedModel` directly, because `InstrumentedModel` owns its request-span lifecycle with no public hook to attach rebar's per-candidate `order`/`outcome`; a rebar-owned child gives that control. Nesting is by ambient OTel context: `instrument_all`'s outer `InstrumentedModel` span is current when `FallbackModel.request` calls each candidate, so the child span parents to it automatically — and because `instrument_all` does NOT re-wrap inner candidates, exactly one rebar span is emitted per candidate (no duplication). A short SPIKE confirms both the child-under-parent nesting and the no-double-wrap property before implementation.

Each candidate span records: zero-based `order`, provider-qualified model identity, an `outcome` from the closed vocabulary {`returned`,`raised`}, and provider-reported usage only when the SDK response exposes it (else omitted, never inferred). Any error text on a `raised` span is placed under the allowlisted `message` key and taken back out sanitized — `sanitize_diagnostic({"message": reason})["message"]` — so no prompt, response, credential, endpoint, or unsanitized body reaches the span. The bug-895c native-to-prompted downgrade needs NO code change here: both the native and prompted `agent.run` route through the SAME wrapped candidates, so the downgrade is already legible as the native attempt's span `raised` (sanitized reason) then the prompted attempt's span `returned`. Instrumentation is best-effort: any exception in candidate wrapping or span emission — tracing enabled or disabled, exporter present or absent — is swallowed at the wrapper boundary so the fallback result, `RunUsage`, and the propagated exception/`FallbackExceptionGroup` are identical to tracing-off. Do not alter `FallbackModel` selection, `ProviderSession` lifecycle, `RunUsage`, `UsageLimits`, pricing, JSONL, or the S2 `_pai_structured` control flow. Provider SDK/HTTP retries stay outside this candidate layer and are never inferred.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — wrap concrete candidate models in the `WrapperModel` subclass at construction, without changing order or fallback predicates.
- `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py` — define the `WrapperModel`-based candidate-span helper: the shared-tracer accessor, the bounded rebar attributes (`order`, model identity, `outcome`, optional usage), and the best-effort swallow.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — thread candidate order/provenance into the wrapper without adding retry policy.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py`, `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — candidate order, outcome, provenance, and usage non-interference.
- `tests/unit/test_candidate_tracing.py` — new focused module using an in-memory OTel span exporter, plus the lean-import and tracing-ON span-failure contracts.

## Testing
- Primary 503 then fallback success: one Agent model-request span parenting two ordered candidate spans (`raised` then `returned`).
- All candidates fail: one `raised` span per attempted candidate; the existing ordered `FallbackExceptionGroup` unchanged.
- Bug-895c downgrade: native attempt span `raised` (sanitized reason) then prompted attempt span `returned`, with no `_pai_structured` change.
- Secret-canary: a candidate whose error carries an API key/email yields a `raised` span whose reason is redacted and which holds no prompt/response/endpoint body.
- Tracing ENABLED with a span-emission/exporter failure: result, usage, and propagated exception identical to tracing-off (span error swallowed).
- Tracing disabled: identical result, usage, imports, and exception behavior.
- Lean-import subprocess: base install without the tracing extra imports and runs with no span dependency error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each attempted fallback candidate emits exactly one rebar OTel span, ordered zero-based, with no duplicate from `instrument_all`; verified by an in-memory exporter test.
- [ ] Every candidate span parents to the single Agent model-request span (ambient-context nesting); verified by parent-span-id assertions.
- [ ] Each candidate span carries provider-qualified model identity; verified by attribute assertions.
- [ ] Each candidate span carries an `outcome` drawn only from {`returned`,`raised`}: the answering model `returned`, each earlier failed candidate `raised`; verified by attribute assertions.
- [ ] The existing ordered `FallbackExceptionGroup` and resolution classification are unchanged by instrumentation; verified by fallback-chain tests.
- [ ] The S2-preserved bug-895c native-to-prompted fallback is legible as a native attempt `raised` then a prompted attempt `returned`, with no change to the `_pai_structured` control flow; verified by a downgrade trace test.
- [ ] A `raised` span reason is redacted through `sanitize_diagnostic` (keyed under `message`) and contains no prompt, response, credential, endpoint secret, or unsanitized exception body; verified by secret-canary assertions.
- [ ] A span-emission or exporter failure while tracing is ENABLED leaves the fallback result, `RunUsage`, and propagated exception identical to tracing-off; verified by a tracing-ON span-failure test.
- [ ] `_usage`, `UsageLimits`, pricing, and durable usage JSONL are identical with tracing on and off and contain no candidate counter; verified by paired-result assertions.
- [ ] The base install without the tracing extra imports and runs with no span dependency error; verified by a lean-import subprocess test.
